_comment_allow: REPLACED defaultMode 'auto' on 2026-08-13. That value was accepted by the settings
parser and then silently never took effect: scripts/hook_context_gate.py reported
'requests auto, running default' on every Write/Edit, so Phase 1's measured 85-88%
prompt reduction had NEVER been observed. A blanket allow is the same policy stated
in a form the matcher honours -- 'deny the destructive, ask the Red row, allow
everything else'. Verified by running, not reading: with allow:[Bash] in force, a
deny rule still blocked and an ask rule still prompted, so the two lists below keep
their teeth. Blanket rather than an enumerated safe-command list on purpose: 201 of
1,185 backtested prompts were unclassifiable compounds, and an enumerated list is
incomplete by construction, so every command not on it keeps prompting -- which is
Residual risk, accepted knowingly and unchanged from the plan: a destructive command
nobody thought to deny. The posture is growing the deny list when something slips,
_comment_deny: Edit(path) rules cover ALL file-editing tools, including Write. The paired
Write(path) entries that used to sit here were silently ignored -- 'claude config
list' names each one -- so config/constitution.md, a Tier 0 file, was blocked
against Edit and reachable by Write. Removed rather than kept as belt-and-braces,
because a rule that does not match is indistinguishable from one that does until
someone tests it. Verified by running: a deny of Edit(./probe_target.txt) refused a
Write to that path, and the file was untouched. Do NOT re-add Write(path) rules.
_comment_ask: The Red tier. Write(./config/agents/*.md) was one of the five silently-ignored Write
rules -- the Edit entry already covers the Write tool.
KNOWN LIMIT, and it is narrower than it was first recorded. Measured 2026-08-13, then
RE-MEASURED BY HAND IN BOTH HARNESSES on 2026-08-14: the split is by TOOL FAMILY, not
by whether a session is interactive.
Edit(...) ask rules DO prompt and DO block in the VS Code panel. Probed on a decoy
file with a throwaway Edit ask rule: the box appeared, was declined, the tool call
aborted, and the file was left byte-unchanged. So all nine Edit rules below have
teeth here and are doing their job.
Bash(...) ask rules do NOT prompt here -- they resolve to ALLOW. Same rule, same
command, same file, minutes apart: iTerm's interactive REPL prompted and NAMED the
rule ('Permission rule Bash(git push *) requires confirmation'); this panel ran it
silently. A human was watching for the box in both. So it is not unattendedness --
the extension never offers a Bash prompt at all.
In a plain-CLI headless session the same prompt auto-DENIES instead, so the two
harnesses still fail in opposite directions.
CONSEQUENCE, applied 2026-08-14: every Bash form of ./deploy.sh moved to deny above
(Mike's decision on H7). It was the only genuinely ungated irreversible action -- a
deploy pushes, SSHs the VM, pulls, pip installs and restarts both units. Lift the deny
deliberately for a real deploy; that edit is the gate now.
git push (below) is knowingly LEFT HERE AND INERT IN THIS PANEL. Denying it would
break /archive step 5, which pushes and then asserts the push landed -- an assertion
added because 11 commits once sat unpushed for six hours. Blast radius is a private
repo, against a close-out ritual that would need a settings edit every single run.
Rule for anyone adding to this list: PROBE PER TOOL FAMILY, never once. This harness
has now produced two tool-family matcher splits in one build -- Edit vs Write in the
deny list (see _comment_deny), and Edit vs Bash here.
